questions.q: Why does a master-detail relationship make load sequencing stricter than a plain lookup relationship?
options: Master-detail relationships are identical to lookups in every respect
A master-detail relationship enforces the parent's existence at the database level, so the child literally cannot be created without the parent already present
Master-detail relationships only apply to standard objects, never custom ones
Master-detail relationships have no bearing on load order at all
questions.explain: Master-detail enforces the relationship at the database level — the child record cannot exist without its parent already present — making correct sequencing mandatory rather than merely advisable.

questions.q: What is a dependency graph used for in migration sequencing?
options: Tracking which users have access to which Salesforce objects
Recording the field-level mapping between source and target
Calculating the total file size of the migration load
Listing every in-scope object and the other in-scope objects it depends on via lookup/master-detail, to determine load order
questions.explain: A dependency graph lists each in-scope object and what it depends on, so objects with no dependencies load first and dependent objects load only after what they reference already exists.

questions.q: What is an "orphaned record," as this lesson defines it?
options: A record that failed to load at all and never entered Salesforce
A record that was deleted using Hard Delete
A record that loaded successfully but isn't actually connected to the parent it was supposed to reference
A record that exists only in a sandbox, never in production
questions.explain: An orphaned record is created when a child loads before its parent exists and the relationship is optional — the record loads (reporting technical success) but with an empty lookup, silently failing to preserve the real relationship.

questions.q: Why does this lesson describe orphaned records as a particularly dangerous failure mode?
options: Because the load often reports as a technical success even though the real-world relationship was silently lost
Because they always cause the entire load job to fail immediately
Because they can only be detected by Salesforce support, never by the project team
Because orphaned records automatically get hard-deleted after 24 hours
questions.explain: Orphaned records are dangerous specifically because the load appears successful (the record was created) while the actual business relationship it was supposed to represent is silently missing.

questions.q: A Contact object has a "Reports To" field that points to another Contact record. What does this lesson say sequencing design has to account for in this case?
options: Nothing extra — self-referencing fields never affect batching
The batching strategy for that object also has to respect the self-referencing dependency, not just dependencies between different objects
The field must be removed from scope entirely before migration can proceed
Self-referencing fields can only be populated through the Data Import Wizard
questions.explain: Sequencing has to think both across objects (parent before child) and, where a self-referencing relationship exists within one object, within that object's own batching strategy too.
